check.notes: The reading is mostly careful: the numbers (4,326 items, o1-preview 42.7 correct and 44.8 F-score), the single-answer scoring and the data-quality check are handled correctly. check.notes: The reading is mostly sound: the numbers (4,326 items; o1-preview 42.7 correct, F-score 44.8), the 'no' format gap, the null cultural asymmetry and the 'noise' treatment of disagreement are defensible. Two things were not challenged. The primary_evaluation_setting quote is the calibration prompt, which does not by itself show zero-shot, though the paper does not describe few-shot prompting. The gold_beyond_stimulus quote is only indirect support, but the value follows from the context-free questions. Treating the third-trainer 94.4% as a data-quality figure rather than a human baseline is also a reasonable choice.

recheck.notes: The reading is sound. All quotes were found verbatim, and the values follow their definitions. The reader's defensible choices include crowd_annotation for the AI trainers (no disciplinary training is stated), single_answer from the scorer, no format gap, and no human baseline (the third-trainer 94.4% is a data-quality check, not a baseline). Reporting accuracy of 42.7 as the best score rather than F-score 44.8 is also defensible and was explained. One weakness: the quote for primary_evaluation_setting (the confidence prompt, p. 7) does not itself show zero-shot, but the paper describes no few-shot or fine-tuned setting for the evaluated models and the field has no not_stated option, so I did not require rework.
